Thanks, Lauren — the proposal looks close to what we discussed. Two items procurement flagged that are deal blockers for Legal and our CFO:

1) MFN / Pricing Parity: we need an MFN-style commitment for the pilot pricing vs. any later published list rates (for 12 months after pilot start). CFO wants assurance we won’t be priced higher than comparable customers in our space for the same capacity profile.

2) Market lock / exclusivity ask: because this is a strategic product integration for Novum (we will route clinical routing through Redwood in the pilot), the business is asking for a short market-lock window where Redwood will not sell product feature parity to direct competitors in the US for 6 months post-pilot.

On benchmark indexing: we want a clause that ties renewal pricing to a market benchmark (index) if adoption scales beyond pilot thresholds — specifically an index cap so price increases are constrained.

These are non-standard for a pilot; procurement asked whether Redwood would consider them in exchange for an enterprise commitment at pilot completion (12–24 month conversion). Please escalate to your commercial leads / legal and let me know the earliest we can get approvals.

Samantha Clark
VP, Product & Partnerships
Novum Health

Lauren — thanks for the heads up and the materials. TL;DR: escalate — this needs an exec signoff and Deal Desk decision on concessions.

Guidance and proposed guardrails:
1) MFN: we can consider a narrow MFN limited to the pilot SKU ("Pilot-Dedicated-3node") and to published list rates for that SKU only, timeboxed to 9–12 months post-pilot start. Exclude promotional/partner programs and channel-specific discounts. Require Novum to provide a specific comparator list for MFN enforcement (this reduces ambiguity).

2) Market-lock / exclusivity: decline broad market-lock. Offer a scoped commercial commitment instead — e.g., a 3-month US field-exclusivity on feature parity for the exact integration, contingent on a signed 12-month committed ARR at a tiered discount. Limit exclusivity geography (US only), vertical (clinical routing), and features (explicit list).

3) Benchmark index: accept an indexed cap approach for renewal if we negotiate the index formula (e.g., CPI + model-inflation cap) and include a floor/ceiling. This prevents open-ended escalations.

4) Commercial offsets: require a minimum 12-month committed ARR (convert pilot) and step-down discount schedule (deeper discount for first 6 months, then revert to standard). Also require a joint QBR cadence and performance SLAs.

Next steps:
- I will draft a recommended concession letter and a narrow redline for Legal to review.
- We should get a quick alignment call with Marissa (GC liaison) and Lauren before sending to Novum.

Marissa — can you take point on Legal redline with the guardrails above? I will draft the commercial concession and an exec summary for VP approval.

Jonas Weber
